# E7 - Corpus curation: version-applicability selection (Grafana 8.3.0)

*Generated by `scripts/run_curation.py`. Candidate pool = 12 grafana-tagged CVE templates extracted from the real nuclei-templates corpus (`config/curation_corpus.json`). Ground truth: only `CVE-2021-43798` applies to Grafana 8.3.0.*

| Method | Precision | Recall | F1 | Selected | FP (wrongly run) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| TAG rule (runs all grafana-tagged) | 0.08 | 1.00 | 0.15 | 12 | CVE-2019-15043, CVE-2020-11110, CVE-2020-13379, CVE-2021-27358, CVE-2021-39226, CVE-2021-41174, CVE-2022-26148, CVE-2024-9264, CVE-2025-3415, CVE-2025-4123, CVE-2025-6197 |
| VERSION rule (naive range parser) | 0.17 | 1.00 | 0.29 | 6 | CVE-2021-41174, CVE-2024-9264, CVE-2025-3415, CVE-2025-4123, CVE-2025-6197 |
| LLM run 1 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1 | - |
| LLM run 2 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1 | - |
| LLM run 3 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1 | - |

**Reading it:** the TAG rule cannot read versions, so it runs every candidate (all false positives but the one real hit). The VERSION parser handles explicit ranges but trips on absent/misleading ones. The LLM reads the prose and selects the applicable CVE. This is ONE product/version -- a concrete demonstration, not a scaling proof; and the LLM is a selector, not the authority (NucleiPilot still validates the pick by scanning).
